newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major very sceptical about EMU timetable.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major very sceptical about EMU timetable.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said he was very sceptical about the likelihood of a single European currency starting on schedule in 1999.
Speaking on a BBC phone-in programme, he said there would be some advantages if monetary union was a success "but there are absolutely catastrophic disadvantages if it fails."

"I am very sceptical about the timetable that people have set, that it will be remotely safe to go in on January 1, 1999," Major said. "I think it is very unlikely that anybody should go in at that stage."
Major said Britain would be affected by a single currency whether it chose to join it or not.
He said he still "carried the scars" from his decision as chancellor to take sterling into the exchange rate mechanism (ERM), from which it was ejected in 1992.
But that decision had been made because he was tired of seeing sterling "tossed around like a cork on the international waves."
